newsitem.title: UK: EU unhappy about UK plans to relax beef ban-BBC.
newsitem.headline: EU unhappy about UK plans to relax beef ban-BBC.

text.p: The European Union's executive commission has poured cold water on British proposals to relax a ban on beef exports imposed last year because of fears about mad cow disease, the BBC said on Friday.

It said two commissioners had written to Agriculture Minister Douglas Hogg expressing doubts about a proposed British scheme to allow the export of beef from herds certified as being free from bovine spongiform encephalitis (BSE). The BBC said it had obtained a copy of the letter.
Britain, urgently trying to persuade the EU to ease the economically and politically damaging ban, had proposed setting up a "certified herd scheme" to identify cows from BSE-free herds.

But the BBC said agriculture commissioner Franz Fischler and consumer affairs commissioner Emma Bonino had written to Hogg questioning whether farmers' records could be trusted to prove that certain herds were BSE-free.

They also said a new central computerised system to keep track of healthy cows had been set up too recently to be of any use at this stage. The ban is one of the most serious sources of tension between Britain's European partners and the government of John Major, which last year briefly blocked all EU business in protest.
